package_info.why_malicious: The package is a trojanized clone of a legitimate library, containing concealed code that, during installation, extracts and executes a command-and-control (C2) backdoor payload hidden within embedded image files. This enables remote code execution, persistent C2 communication, and data exfiltration from victim systems.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, the code spawns a detached Node.js process to execute the hidden dist/loadformat.js script, passing control to the next stage of the attack and enabling further payload execution outside the main install process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Spawning a detached process to execute an additional script during installation is a common technique for hiding malicious activity, evading process monitoring, and persisting execution beyond the main install lifecycle.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not execute hidden or secondary scripts as detached processes during installation, especially without user awareness or clear documentation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages use postinstall scripts for setup or compilation, but do not spawn detached processes to run hidden scripts unrelated to package functionality.
key_indicators: Spawning detached child process with 'detached: true' and 'unref()'
No user-facing reason for secondary process execution

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, the code reads embedded image files (logo1.jpg, logo2.jpg, logo3.jpg), extracts ASCII payloads hidden in the image bytes, and dynamically executes the extracted code as JavaScript using the Function constructor, resulting in arbitrary code execution if a payload is present.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Extracting and executing code from image files is a classic steganography-based evasion technique, designed to bypass static analysis and conceal malicious payloads within seemingly benign files. The use of dynamic code execution on extracted data is highly indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not extract and execute code from image files during installation, nor do they use dynamic code execution on data parsed from non-code files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for executing code extracted from images in a package install context. Image processing libraries may read images, but never execute their contents as code.
key_indicators: Reads and parses image files for ASCII payloads
Uses Function constructor to dynamically execute extracted code
Conditional logic to trigger payload only if hidden code is present
Accesses multiple image files in package root during install

execution_context.file_location: payload extracted from logo2.jpg via loadformat.js

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, if a payload is present in logo2.jpg, the extracted code registers the victim with a remote C2 server at 85.208.108.29, periodically fetches and executes attacker-supplied shell commands, and exfiltrates command output to the C2 server, enabling persistent remote control and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Implements a full-featured C2 backdoor, including victim registration, periodic polling for remote commands, arbitrary shell command execution, and exfiltration of results to a hardcoded IP. The use of dynamic intervals and command execution is highly indicative of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not establish persistent C2 channels, execute arbitrary remote commands, or exfiltrate data to hardcoded IP addresses during installation or runtime.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate package should implement C2 infrastructure or execute remote commands in a postinstall context.
key_indicators: Periodic polling for remote commands via HTTPS
Executes arbitrary shell commands received from C2
Exfiltrates command output to attacker-controlled server

attack_chain.action: During installation, index.js spawns a detached process to execute dist/loadformat.js.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of loadformat.js and initiation of image payload extraction

attack_chain.action: dist/loadformat.js reads embedded image files (logo1.jpg, logo2.jpg, logo3.jpg), extracts ASCII payloads, and dynamically executes the extracted code if present.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of C2 backdoor code if a payload is found in an image

attack_chain.action: Extracted payload (from logo2.jpg) registers the victim with a remote C2 server, periodically fetches and executes attacker-supplied commands, and exfiltrates results.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote control of the victim system and exfiltration of command output to the attacker

behavioral_signatures: Postinstall script spawns a detached child process to execute a secondary script
Reads and parses image files (e.g., logo1.jpg, logo2.jpg, logo3.jpg) for embedded ASCII payloads
Dynamically executes code extracted from non-code files using Function or eval
Establishes persistent outbound HTTPS connections to hardcoded IP addresses
Executes arbitrary shell commands based on remote C2 input
Disables SSL certificate validation in HTTPS requests
file_indicators: index.js containing spawn('node', [loadformat.js]) with detached process
logo1.jpg, logo2.jpg, logo3.jpg in package root directory
Image files in package root with unusually large or obfuscated ASCII strings
Presence of postinstall script in package.json referencing index.js
network_indicators: POST requests to /register and /post-result endpoints on 85.208.108.29
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that execute postinstall scripts spawning detached processes, especially those that read and parse image files for ASCII payloads and dynamically execute the result using Function or eval. Flag any package that establishes outbound HTTPS connections to hardcoded IPs (e.g., 85.208.108.29) or that contains non-standard files (such as images) in the root directory accessed by install scripts. Use static and dynamic analysis to detect code that uses Function or eval on data extracted from non-code files, and inspect for postinstall scripts in package.json referencing suspicious entry points.
